request.prompt: Create one production candidate bitmap for the Armax Relay Clash 2D fighting-game art catalog, faithfully studying the supplied original game-model reference. A single full-body subject only, isolated on a genuinely transparent RGBA background, no scenery, no floor plane or ground shadow, no lettering, no caption, no border, no diagram, no contact sheet, no repeated views, no logo added outside the subject. Clean readable silhouette, detailed realistic game-model materials, restrained neutral studio illumination. Show a three-quarter front view with the subject oriented toward screen-right, camera level and minimal perspective distortion. The complete head, equipment, limbs and feet must fit; leave at least six percent transparent breathing room on every side. Preserve the reference's real anatomy, panel construction, proportions, asymmetric equipment and exact costume palette. Do not redesign or modernize. Subject: the standard Cerberus Assault Trooper from Mass Effect 3, exactly as the three views in the reference. Fully enclosed stocky adult armored human soldier. Weathered off-white/light-grey armor, limited mustard-yellow chest and shoulder blocks and yellow vertical markings on forearms/thighs, black woven undersuit and black central belly, heavy white chest plates above the circular recessed abdominal joint, white hip belt. Preserve the peculiar dark rounded helmet with its raised vertical central panel, thin angular red optic strips along the cheek/eye edges, two round grey respirator filters on the lower sides and pale lower jaw armor. Small asymmetrical shoulder backpack blocks, segmented arms, white rounded thigh shells, circular knees, black shin recesses and split toe boots. Carry the EXACT compact long straight angular firearm visible in the source low at the ANATOMICAL RIGHT side, muzzle down, the other arm relaxed, no aiming or firing. No Guardian shield, no N7 marks, no extra yellow paint. Calm alert feet-apart stance with complete gun and boots in frame. Preserve front panel seams and proportions rather than inventing generic sci-fi armor.
